story:
The minstrels say Lichas was Merlin's pupil, the last one, who stayed behind under the stones to keep a door when his master went away, and that his master said he would not be long. That was before Camlann. Lichas is still keeping it. He has gone to bone and spite in the keeping, and he asks every living visitor the same thing: whether the master sent them.

He has not kept it alone. In a hall of the upper barrows that the soul harvesters leave alone he keeps a school of the dead: spiritual advisors who have nobody left to advise, followers who repented of whatever they did when it was too late to matter, phantoms who listen. He teaches them, though no one living has heard what, and the repentant stand nearest him, as pupils do, and rise with him.

Elvinia Dareal of Caer Witrin says Lichas is not keeping a door shut but holding one ajar, and that the hollow man Dathmul in Snowdonia and the scroll Vera Astyrian guards are pieces of the same gathering; she wants him destroyed for it. Dafydd of the harp says Lichas is only tired. Both may be true. A pupil left too long stops waiting for his master and starts waiting for someone else.
legend: Wizard Lichas, level 48, upper west halls of the Barrows, in the middle of his school: spiritual advisors, repentant followers (37) and malefic phantoms, all undead and they help each other. Clear the room from the edge, then kill him; he has no spells in the data, he just hits. Feast of the Decadent wants him destroyed after Dathmul and Vera Astyrian's scroll. Respawn about five minutes.

lairEntry: A wizard teaching the dead. They stand when he does.
